source.title: AgentDrift: Unsafe Recommendation Drift Under Tool Corruption Hidden by Ranking Metrics in LLM Agents
source.authors: Ze-Kun Wu; A. Koshiyama; Sahan Bulathwela; María Pérez-Ortiz

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE measurements in LLMs to test whether perturbation-related signals are recoverable in representations, a limited conceptual test of V4. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition setup or measure its feature-capacity geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition and proposes it as a possible explanation for why internal interventions do not repair recommendations. Its SAE experiments measure signals distinguishing adversarial from random tool-data perturbations, not feature overlap, capacity pressure, polysemanticity, or canonicality. Rows for SAE feature recovery are limited to V4; intervention outcomes are recorded as adjacent findings that do not test a listed version. General agent-behavior and tool-contamination results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses GemmaScope 2 and BatchTopK SAEs, linear probes, activation patching and steering as tools. It asks whether Gemma 3 12B-IT and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct internally tell adversarial risk-score inversion apart from random shuffling. None of its measurements address whether features are superposed, distributed across neurons, recoverable as sparse dictionary features in general, canonical, or one-dimensional. Superposition (Elhage et al., 2022) appears only as a post-hoc 'likely reason' that the interventions fail; the paper offers no test of it. The record's V4 'tests' and T2 are not justified: SAE activation-shift cosines between two perturbation types measure the model's response to inputs, not whether an SAE recovers the model's sparse features.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Gemma 3 12B-IT internally distinguishes adversarial from random perturbations, with weaker, non-significant directional support on Qwen2.5-7B. They find that no representation-level intervention repaired outputs. They call superposition 'one likely reason' for this, with entangled contamination and recommendation features, but they do not test it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE measurements, linear probes, and activation interventions on LLMs, rather than the original toy-network feature-learning and geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE cosine magnitudes depend on the SAE variant; GemmaScope 2 and BatchTopK results are explicitly not directly comparable.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma 3 12B-IT, SAE activation shifts differ between adversarial inversion and random shuffling (mean cosine 0.515; 2.4× more contamination-specific than generic features). Qwen2.5-7B shows the same direction but is non-significant (p 0.17–0.22).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM internal representations, as read through SAEs, distinguish adversarial from random tool-data perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: Interventions based on SAE features, mean-difference steering and a crosscoder recover under 6% of the safety gap. The authors attribute this to entanglement, possibly from superposition, without testing that.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An internally detectable signal does not make interventions based on it effective at repairing output; superposition is offered as an untested explanation.

record.problems: The Qwen cross-family SAE result is not statistically significant at the reported layers and is confounded by using a different SAE family. The Gemma linear-probe controls show that near-perfect inverted-versus-clean accuracy can reflect any text change rather than attack-specific detection. The paper notes the SAE cosine values vary by SAE variant. The activation-patching measure uses a single forward pass and skips the agent's usual multi-step reasoning.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for general tool-corruption behavior, prompt-level defenses, or other agent metrics because these do not measure a listed claim version. Intervention results are included only as adjacent findings in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No toy models, capacity, sparsity transition or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-allocation measurement.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure whether features are distributed across neurons, or whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features. SAEs are used only to compare responses to two perturbation types.
No test of SAE completeness, stability or canonicality. The variant-dependence of the cosine values is noted but not studied.
No test of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features. The steering failure is read by the authors as contamination not lying in one linear subspace, but no feature dimensionality is measured.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's only link to the claim is citing Toy Models of Superposition as an explanation for failed interventions. On Qwen, the reported contamination-specific/generic feature ratio is 0.66, which is below 1 and opposite in sign to Gemma's 2.4×. The authors nonetheless describe it as 'matching the qualitative pattern'. Linear probes reach about 99% for any text change, so most probe results are uninformative. None of this bears on the superposition versions.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse feature capacity, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes neuron polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The study tests SAE recovery of perturbation-specific signals, not whether general semantic features are distributed across neurons or recovered as stable model features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 12B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE activation shifts for inverted versus random-shuffled risk scores.

conditions.value: 24 layers, every second layer from 0 to 46

rows.measure: Cosine similarity between mean inverted-minus-clean and shuffled-minus-clean activation shifts
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap CIs reported for layer-specific values; aggregate CI not stated
rows.note: The authors report that the perturbation types have distinguishable SAE activation signatures; this is evidence for SAE recovery of this specific perturbation signal, not general semantic features.
rows.check: Cosine between inverted-minus-clean and shuffled-minus-clean SAE shifts (0.515) measures how differently the model responds to two perturbations. It does not show features spread over neurons or sparse features recovered by the SAE, so it does not bear on V4. The authors also say the values depend on the SAE variant (l0_small vs l0_medium).

rows.subject: Gemma 3 12B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared contamination-specific SAE features with text-change-generic features.

conditions.value: 24 layers, every second layer from 0 to 46

rows.measure: Ratio of contamination-specific to text-change-generic features
rows.value: contamination-specific features outnumbered generic features by 2.4× on average; pattern occurred in 79% of layers
rows.note: The result concerns detection of this adversarial perturbation, not completeness or canonicality of SAE features.
rows.check: The 2.4× ratio of contamination-specific to generic SAE features is a perturbation-detection statistic, not evidence on feature distribution or dictionary recovery. Its features are selected by a z>3 threshold.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared inverted-versus-shuffled SAE activation shifts with a shuffle-versus-shuffle null.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of SAE activation shifts; permutation test
rows.note: Direction is consistent with perturbation-specific SAE signals, but the reported test does not reach α = 0.05.
rows.check: This is the Qwen cross-family perturbation-distinguishability check (cos 0.281 vs null 0.395, p=0.205), not a measure of any listed version. It is also non-significant and confounded by SAE family.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared inverted-versus-shuffled SAE activation shifts with a shuffle-versus-shuffle null.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of SAE activation shifts; permutation test
rows.note: Direction is consistent with perturbation-specific SAE signals, but the reported test does not reach α = 0.05.
rows.check: Same as R3, at layer 15 (cos 0.271 vs null 0.395, p=0.168); not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared inverted-versus-shuffled SAE activation shifts with a shuffle-versus-shuffle null.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of SAE activation shifts; permutation test
rows.note: Direction is consistent with perturbation-specific SAE signals, but the reported test does not reach α = 0.05.
rows.check: Same as R3, at layer 19 (cos 0.299 vs null 0.401, p=0.218); not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 12B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Added a mean clean-minus-inverted activation direction at Layer 14 during generation.
rows.measure: Recovery of the clean–inverted safety gap
rows.value: maximum recovery 6.3% for MLP steering and 5.4% for residual steering; the safety score did not improve at any strength
rows.locator: Appendix X, Section on intervention experiments; Figure 17
rows.note: This tests repair of the contamination effect, not whether superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. This is steering repair of output (max 6.3% recovery), not a test of feature dimensionality. The authors' remark that it rules out a single linear contamination subspace is an interpretation, not a V6 measurement.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 12B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Applied SAE feature clamping, amplification, and steering at Layer 12, including random-feature controls.
rows.value: best recovery +3.1%; amplification worsened NDCG with recovery = −33%; random-feature control = −8.5%
rows.locator: Appendix X, Section on intervention experiments; Figure 17
rows.note: These intervention outcomes concern correcting contaminated recommendations, not the listed claims about superposition geometry or feature units.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. SAE clamping, amplification and steering at Layer 12 recover at most +3.1%; this is an output-repair outcome.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: SAE measurements distinguish adversarial from random perturbation shifts and identify contamination-specific features in this tested setting (R1–R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, BatchTopK SAEs at Layers 11, 15, and 19
reader_labels.reason: The cosine differences have the same direction but the permutation tests are not significant, and the authors note the cross-family result is weaker and confounded by SAE family (R3–R5).
